title: Private Network: Firewall & Peering Checklist for Enterprise Onboarding
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Purpose

This document is a practical, sequence-driven checklist to validate network, firewall, and peering configurations during enterprise private deployment onboarding (VPC and on-prem). It consolidates recommended rules, verification steps, and escalation paths to minimize go-live delays caused by connectivity issues between customer networks and Redwood Inference Private control and data planes.

Audience

- Customer network and security teams
- Redwood Solutions Engineering (SE) and Customer Success (CS) onboarding leads
- Redwood Private deployment engineers

Scope and intent

This checklist covers:
- Outbound and inbound firewall rules for control plane and data plane services
- VPC peering and route validation patterns
- Basic NAT and proxy considerations
- Diagnostic commands and test vectors to validate traffic flows
- Acceptance criteria and how to escalate unresolved issues

Summary of assumptions

1. Customer environment: VPC (AWS/Azure/GCP) or equivalent private network with ability to add routes/security-group/firewall rules.
2. Customer will provide a network contact, CIDR ranges, and preferred peering method (VPC peering, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink, VPN, or dedicated circuit).
3. Private deployment uses two logical planes: control-plane endpoints (API/management) and data-plane endpoints (inference endpoints, egress to telemetry).

Network ownership and run roles

- Customer network owner: single point-of-contact for rule changes and routing (required).
- Redwood SE onboarding lead: coordinates validation steps and performs Redwood-side checks.
- Redwood Private ops: accepts packet captures / logs and performs further investigation when escalated.

Checklist: Pre-provision (customer to confirm before scheduling provisioning)

1) Provide required values (email these to SE):
   - Primary VPC CIDR(s) and subnets (e.g., 10.100.0.0/16)
   - NAT / egress architecture details (NAT Gateway or egress proxies)
   - Peering preference: VPC Peering / Transit Gateway / PrivateLink / VPN / Direct Connect
   - Egress to 3rd-party KMS or identity provider endpoints (if used)
   - Internal DNS resolution strategy (will customer resolve Redwood hostnames internally?)

2) Schedule a 60m network validation call with network owners and Redwood SE.

Firewall and routing rules (required)

Apply these rules to customer perimeter firewalls / security groups / network appliances. Replace example CIDRs and hostnames with the values provided by Redwood in the deployment manifest.

| Purpose | Protocol | Direction | Destination / Port | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Control plane API (management) | TCP | Outbound | redwood-control.example.com:443 | TLS 1.2+; allow SNI "redwood-control.example.com" |
| Data plane inference endpoints | TCP | Outbound / Peered | 10.200.0.0/22:443 | Customer should allow peered subnet range for inference requests |
| KV cache and internal telemetry | TCP | Outbound | 10.201.0.0/24:443 | Encryption required; avoid deep packet inspection |
| Healthcheck probes (from Redwood) | TCP | Inbound (when enabled) | <customer-health-probe-ip>:443 | Optional; customer may whitelist Redwood probe IPs |
| NTP (time sync) | UDP | Outbound | 0.pool.ntp.org:123 or NTP server IPs | Time skew > 2s can break TLS session validation |
| DNS resolution | UDP/TCP | Outbound | <customer-dns-ips>:53 | If private DNS resolvers used, confirm recursive replies for redwood hostnames |

Note: If the deployment uses PrivateLink/Private Endpoint, data-plane traffic does not require NATed egress but still requires Security Group/ACL rules permitting the private endpoint.

Peering and route validation

- VPC Peering: Ensure both sides have explicit route table entries for each other's CIDRs pointing to the peering attachment. No overlapping CIDRs allowed.
- Transit Gateway: Confirm route propagation and attachment associations include the subnets in scope.
- VPN / Direct Connect: Verify BGP prefixes and BGP session state are UP (use show ip bgp summary / cloud console BGP diagnostics).
- PrivateLink: Validate ENI creation in the customer subnet and that security groups allow traffic to the service endpoint.

Test vectors and verification steps (execute with SE)

1) DNS validation
   - From a host in-customer-VPC: nslookup redwood-control.example.com <customer-dns-ip>
   - Expected: resolves to Redwood-provided control-plane IPs (or private endpoint IPs)

2) TCP handshake and TLS validation
   - curl -v --resolve 'redwood-control.example.com:443:<ip>' https://redwood-control.example.com/health
   - Expected: HTTP 200 and a valid TLS certificate matching the hostname. If certificate is customer-mTLS, provide client certs.

3) Peering route test (ICMP/TCP)
   - ping <data-plane-ip> (if ICMP allowed) or 
   - nc -vz <data-plane-ip> 443
   - Expected: connection establishes within 50ms for same-region peering or within agreed latency SLO.

4) End-to-end inference call test
   - curl -X POST https://<inference-host>/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"ping"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
   - Expected: 200 with model response; token auth validated. Record request latency and token usage.

5) Telemetry and metrics egress
   - Confirm outbound connectivity to telemetry endpoints (if using SaaS telemetry) or ensure logs are forwarded to provided collector address.

Acceptance criteria (must be green to proceed to provisioning)

- Control-plane API resolves and TLS handshake succeeds from a customer-hosted instance.
- Data-plane CIDRs are routable across peering attachment and security groups allow TCP/443.
- End-to-end inference call completes successfully from a customer test VM.
- Time synchronization is within tolerance (+/- 2s).
- Agreed monitoring/probe IPs are whitelisted if customer requires inbound probes.

Common failure modes and quick mitigations

1) DNS resolves to public IP but customer expected private endpoint
   - Cause: split-horizon DNS not configured or DNS forwarding missing.
   - Mitigation: Update private DNS zone with records provided by Redwood or configure conditional forwarding to Redwood DNS resolver.

2) Connection times out to data plane IP
   - Cause: Route table missing peering route or security group denying egress.
   - Mitigation: Validate route table entries and security group/ACLs; run traceroute to identify hop where packets drop.

3) TLS handshake fails with certificate name mismatch
   - Cause: using IP address instead of hostname or incorrect SNI through proxy.
   - Mitigation: Use hostname in SNI; update proxy to forward Host header and SNI.

4) Intermittent failures under load
   - Cause: asymmetric routing, stateful firewall timeouts, or SNAT port exhaustion.
   - Mitigation: Use connection tracking tuning, increase ephemeral port range, or enable NAT gateway autoscaling patterns.

Diagnostic commands matrix (copy/paste friendly)

- DNS: dig +short redwood-control.example.com @<customer-dns>
- TLS: openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername redwood-control.example.com
- TCP: nc -vz <ip> 443
- Traceroute: traceroute <ip> (Linux) / tracert <ip> (Windows)
- BGP: (on-customer-router) show ip bgp summary

Escalation path (when checklist verification fails)

1) Network owner coordinates immediate troubleshooting with Redwood SE during the validation call.
2) If unresolved within 60 minutes, SE opens a Customer Incident with level: "network-blocking" and notifies Redwood Private Ops.
3) Private Ops will collect packet capture (pcap) from both sides where possible and run a 1:1 session diagnostic. (Provide pcap, timestamps, and test vectors.)
4) If vendor appliance or carrier issue suspected (Transit GW, Direct Connect), escalate to cloud provider support with session history and BGP details.

On-call and SLAs

- Redwood will aim to respond to network-blocking incidents within 30 minutes during business hours and 60 minutes outside business hours per the Enterprise onboarding commitment.
- Target resolution time depends on root cause: misconfiguration (<= 8 hours), provider/carrier (<72 hours with provider support).

Customer checklist sign-off (to be completed by customer network owner)

1) I confirm the fields in the provisioning manifest are accurate.
2) I confirm the firewall and route table entries listed above are applied and verified.
3) I confirm the end-to-end inference test succeeded and recorded latency is within acceptable bounds.

Signed: _______________________  Name: _______________________  Date: _______________________

Appendix: Example iptables rules (customer Linux NAT host)

# Allow outbound TLS to Redwood control plane
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d <redwood-control-ip> --dport 443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
# Allow established/related inbound for return traffic
iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

Appendix: When using an egress proxy (common enterprise pattern)

- Ensure SNI passthrough (not SNI rewrite) for redwood-control.example.com or configure explicit proxy bypass for the Redwood control/data-plane domains.
- If mTLS is used, ensure the proxy allows client certificate forwarding or use a sidecar that terminates mTLS locally and forwards plaintext to the proxy only within the VPC.
